newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemeni forces tighten grip on Germans' kidnappers.
newsitem.headline: Yemeni forces tighten grip on Germans' kidnappers.

text.p: Yemeni security forces on Saturday tightened their noose on tribesmen holding four German tourists hostage in the country's rugged interior, official sources said.
"Security forces have been reinforced to tighten the military siege around the kidnappers in the area of Al-Mehjezah in the Marib region," an official told Reuters.
The mountainous Marib governorate is in eastern Yemen.
"Additional forces were sent to the area from Marib itself as well as from Sanaa," he added.
The German foreign ministry on Friday said the four tourists -- two men and two women -- had been abducted on Thursday.
A Yemeni Interior Ministry official said they were kidnapped by "destructive elements" while returning from Marib to the capital Sanaa.
He stressed that the abductors were bent on tarnishing Yemen's image and said the authorities "would not take it easy with these types of destructive element".

Earlier this month, a group of seven German tourists on a motorcycle tour in Yemen were also kidnapped. They were held hostage by Yemeni tribesmen and released unharmed after more than a week in captivity.
The German foreign ministry said crisis centres had been set up in Bonn and at the German embassy in Sanaa to deal with the latest kidnapping.

In recent years, Yemeni tribes with grievances against the government or foreign oil firms have kidnapped scores of tourists, diplomats and other foreigners to use as bargaining chips. The hostages were all released unharmed.

Marib has been the site of previous hostage takings. A U.S. engineer kidnapped by Yemeni tribemen in Marib was released in February after 16 days in captivity. A French diplomat was also kidnapped in Marib in October and set free two weeks later.
